message.content: {"summary":"You submitted a well-researched, balanced ethics report with compelling ethical analysis and strong real-world case studies. Your introduction thoroughly maps out stakeholder interests and organisational contexts. To improve, broaden your recommendations to provide explicit guidance across external stakeholders, integrate supporting visual elements such as summary tables or decision flowcharts, and align your operational recommendations with Rachel's specific organizational authority as a QA engineer.","next_steps":["Broaden your final recommendations to provide distinct, actionable decision-making guidance for external stakeholders such as the client and chip contractor, rather than focusing solely on Rachel.","Integrate competent visual elements, such as stakeholder impact matrices or ethical decision-tree diagrams, to support your narrative.","Tailor Rachel's recommended actions to her actual professional scope (e.g., withholding QA sign-off and escalating to executive leadership rather than unilaterally refusing contracts)."],"criteria":{"C1":"You achieved Excellent by clearly framing the ethical dilemmas within engineering design and organisational contexts while thoroughly identifying affected stakeholders and broad societal impacts in your INTRODUCTION.","C2":"Your discussion objectively weighed the arguments for and against shipping in depth. To reach Excellent, expand beyond Rachel's immediate actions in the RECOMMENDATION section to provide explicit decision-making recommendations for several distinct stakeholders, including external parties like the client and contractor.","C3":"You built a compelling, well-structured argument connecting technical trade-offs to the Engineers Australia Code of Ethics. To attain Excellent, ensure your arguments demonstrate a systematic, exhaustive understanding of the ethical dilemmas across all identified stakeholders.","C4":"You substantiated your claims well using relevant references and case studies (such as the NHS IT failure and Volkswagen). To reach Excellent, integrate more balanced quantitative data alongside your qualitative evidence to deepen your empirical support.","C5":"Your report was logically structured and fluent. To move from Good to Very Good or Excellent, incorporate relevant visual elements (e.g., comparison tables or framework figures) and proofread carefully to eliminate typographical errors like 'DICUSSION'."}}
